sentences.text: Buchanosteus was a member of the class Placodermi, an extinct group of armored fish.
This genus belongs to the family Buchanosteidae.
The type species of the genus Buchanosteus is Buchanosteus confertituberculatus, described by Chapman in 1916.
A species named Buchanosteus nuricus was described by Mark-Kurik in 2004.
A species named Buchanosteus guangxiensis was described by Wang in 2005.
B. nuricus is anatomically very similar to B. confertituberculatus.
These fish lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in Early Devonian marine strata across Asia and Australia.
The type species, B. confertituberculatus, is known from the Emsian-aged Taemas-Weejasper Reef in modern-day New South Wales, Australia.
It lived alongside other buchanosteid genera in the same area.
B. guangxianensis is known mainly from an incomplete endocranium found in Pragian-aged deposits near Guangxi, China.
